questions.question: According to Constitution of India a governor can be appointed _________

options.text: for a single state at a time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**for two or more states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Article 153 of the Constitution of India, there shall be a Governor for each state.
 
• The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as the governor for two or more states.
 
• This provision allows for administrative efficiency and the reduction of administrative costs.
 
• The President of India appoints the Governor, who holds office during the pleasure of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 153**

 
 
• Article 153 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Governor for each State.
 
• However, the same Article also allows the appointment of a single person as Governor for two or more states.
 
 
 
• **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956**
 
 
• This amendment was introduced to reorganize states on a linguistic basis.
 
• It also included a provision allowing the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states.
 
• This was primarily for administrative convenience and to reduce costs.
 
 
 
• **Role and Functions of a Governor**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the nominal head of a state, similar to how the President functions at the central level.
 
• The Governor's duties include appointing the Chief Minister, summoning and proroguing the state legislature, and giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• The Governor also has discretionary powers that can be exercised as per their discretion or as directed by the President.
 
 
 
• **Appointment and Tenure**
 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The usual term of a Governor is five years, but they can be removed earlier by the President.
 
• There are no specified qualifications for the appointment of a Governor, but the person should be an Indian citizen and should have completed the age of 35 years.

questions.question: Credit of invention of the Chess game goes to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The game of chess is believed to have originated in India during the Gupta Empire in the 6th century AD.
 
• It was initially called "Chaturanga," which means "four divisions of the military" - infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots, which are represented by the pieces that would evolve into the modern pawn, knight, bishop, and rook, respectively.
 
• The game spread from India to Persia, where it became known as "Shatranj."
 
• From Persia, the game spread to the Islamic world and then to Europe, where it evolved into the modern game of chess we know today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chaturanga:**

 
 
• Chaturanga is an ancient Indian strategy game that is considered the ancestor of chess.
 
• The game simulates a battle, with each type of piece representing different military units.
 
• The objective of the game was similar to that of chess - to checkmate the opponent's king.
 
 
 
• **Shatranj:**
 
 
• Shatranj is the Persian adaptation of Chaturanga, which was played in the medieval Islamic world.
 
• Shatranj introduced several changes to the original game, including new rules and the renaming of pieces.
 
• The game of Shatranj is very similar to modern chess, with some differences in the movement of pieces.
 
 
 
• **Evolution to Modern Chess:**
 
 
• As the game spread to Europe, it underwent several transformations.
 
• The modern rules of chess began to take shape in Spain and Italy during the 15th century.
 
• The game continued to evolve, with the introduction of the queen's powerful movement and the standardization of the rules in the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Chess in the Modern World:**
 
 
• Today, chess is a global game played by millions of people worldwide.
 
• It is recognized as a sport and has a well-organized system of tournaments and championships.
 
• The game is also used as a tool for educational purposes, promoting critical thinking, strategy, and cognitive skills.

questions.question: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme with an outlay of __________ to boost availability of disease-free and quality planting material for high value horticultural crops.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs 2,200 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme.
 
• The programme has an outlay of Rs 2,200 crore.
 
• It aims to boost the availability of disease-free and quality planting material for high value horticultural crops.
 
• This initiative is part of the larger Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) campaign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India)**

 
 
• It is a vision of the Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi of making India a self-reliant nation.
 
• It aims to make the country and its citizens independent and self-reliant in all senses.
 
• The initiative focuses on five pillars: economy, infrastructure, system, vibrant demography, and demand.
 
• Various schemes and policies have been introduced under this initiative to promote local manufacturing, reduce dependency on imports, and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Horticulture**
 
 
• Horticulture is the branch of agriculture that deals with the art, science, technology, and business of plant cultivation.
 
• This includes the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, herbs, sprouts, mushrooms, algae, flowers, seaweeds, and non-food crops such as grass and ornamental trees and plants.
 
• Horticultural crops are diverse; they include annual and perennial species, fruits and vegetables, and decorative indoor plants.
 
• Horticulture plays a vital role in the economy by providing employment opportunities and contributing significantly to the GDP.
 
 
 
• **Disease-Free Planting Material**
 
 
• Disease-free planting material refers to plants or plant parts that are free from pathogens and pests that can cause diseases.
 
• The use of such material is crucial in horticulture to ensure healthy crop production and high yields.
 
• It helps in reducing the spread of diseases, ensuring the production of quality crops, and increasing the overall productivity of the horticultural sector.
 
• Programs like the Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme aim to promote the use of disease-free planting material to enhance agricultural productivity and sustainability.

questions.question: The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas (2nd century BCE to 3rd century CE) is known in Indian history as the _________ period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Post-Mauryan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas is referred to as the **Post-Mauryan period**.
 
• This era spanned from the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
 
• It was a time of significant political fragmentation and the rise of several regional kingdoms in India.
 
• The Post-Mauryan period saw the growth of new trade routes, the spread of Buddhism and Jainism, and the flourishing of arts and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maurya Empire**

 
 
• The Maurya Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE, was one of the largest and most powerful political and military empires in ancient India.
 
• It reached its zenith under Emperor Ashoka, who ruled from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• Ashoka is renowned for his propagation of Buddhism and his efforts to spread Buddhist values and ethics across his empire and beyond.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire was established by Sri Gupta around the early 4th century CE.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India due to the significant achievements in arts, science, and literature during this period.
 
• Prominent rulers like Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II led the empire to its peak.
 
 
 
• **Regional Kingdoms**
 
 
• During the Post-Mauryan period, several regional kingdoms emerged, including the Shungas, Satavahanas, Kushanas, and others.
 
• The Shungas, who succeeded the Mauryas in the Magadha region, were known for their patronage of Brahmanism and the revival of Hindu rituals and practices.
 
• The Satavahanas ruled in the Deccan region and played a crucial role in promoting trade and commerce.
 
• The Kushanas, originating from Central Asia, established a powerful empire in northwestern India and parts of Central Asia, promoting both Buddhism and Hinduism.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Economic Developments**
 
 
• The Post-Mauryan period witnessed extensive trade routes connecting India with Central Asia, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean world.
 
• Buddhism and Jainism continued to spread, with many monasteries and stupas being built during this time.
 
• Art and architecture flourished, with notable contributions in the form of Gandhara and Mathura school of arts.

questions.question: The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951, which was the ____________ census in its continuous series.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eighth**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The census is a regular and systematic collection of data about the population.
 
• India has a long tradition of conducting the census, which started in 1872.
 
• The 1881 Census is considered the first complete census in India, marking the start of the continuous decennial census series under British colonial administration.
 
• The first census after India gained independence was conducted in 1951.
 
• This 1951 census was the eighth census in the continuous series that started in 1881.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census:**

 
 
• A census is the procedure of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• It is a regular practice in many countries and typically takes place every 10 years.
 
• The data collected during a census can include information on various demographic, social, and economic characteristics.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and policy-making purposes.
 
 
 
• **History of Census in India:**
 
 
• The first complete census was taken in 1881, and since then, censuses have been undertaken uninterruptedly once every ten years.
 
• The census operations are organized under the Census Act of 1948.
 
• The responsibility for conducting the census lies with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• The census data serves as a critical input for various government schemes and programs.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census:**
 
 
• The census provides a snapshot of the population's size, distribution, and demographic characteristics.
 
• It helps in the allocation of government resources and representation in legislative bodies.
 
• The data aids in the planning and implementation of public policies and services such as healthcare, education, and transportation.
 
• The census also assists businesses in market research and strategic planning.
 
 
 
• **1951 Census:**
 
 
• The 1951 Census was the first census conducted after India gained independence.
 
• It marked the beginning of a new era in the collection of demographic data in India.
 
• The census provided valuable information about the population, including details on migration, literacy rates, and employment.
 
• This data was crucial for the country's planning and development initiatives during the early years of independence.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan of India was known as the "Mahalanobis Plan"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan of India, spanning from 1956 to 1961, is commonly known as the "Mahalanobis Plan" after the prominent Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.
 
• It focused on the rapid industrialization of the country, particularly emphasizing the development of the heavy industries sector.
 
• The plan aimed to establish a socialist pattern of society by prioritizing public sector investments and reducing inequalities in income and wealth.
 
• Under this plan, the Indian government sought to achieve self-sufficiency in essential goods and services and reduce dependence on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)**

 
 
• It focused on the agricultural sector with the aim of improving food production.
 
• The primary objective was to address the immediate food crisis and lay the foundation for future economic growth.
 
• Significant investments were made in irrigation, power, and transport infrastructure.
 
• The plan was relatively successful and achieved a growth rate of around 3.6% annually.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)**
 
 
• This plan aimed at making India self-reliant and self-generating economy.
 
• The focus was on agriculture to ensure that the country had enough food supplies.
 
• It also emphasized on the expansion of the basic industries and the diversification of the industrial structure.
 
• The plan faced challenges due to the Indo-China war in 1962 and the Indo-Pakistani war in 1965, leading to a financial crunch.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)**
 
 
• The primary aim of this plan was growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
 
• Emphasis was placed on the Green Revolution to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains production.
 
• It focused on strengthening the infrastructure and improving the standard of living for the citizens.
 
• Despite some progress, the plan was marred by issues such as inflation and economic instability.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question:
Which of the following statement is 'true' for ‘dobereiner's triads'?

I. Triads were in order of atomic masses.

II. Atomic mass of middle element was roughly the average of atomic masses of other two elements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dobereiner's triads were groups of three elements.
 
• The elements in each triad were ordered by their atomic masses.
 
• The atomic mass of the middle element was roughly the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
 
• Dobereiner's triads were an early attempt to classify elements based on their properties and atomic masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dobereiner's Triads**

 
 
• Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner was a German chemist who, in the early 19th century, observed that certain groups of three elements (which he called "triads") had similar chemical properties and that the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
 
• Examples of Dobereiner's triads include:
 
 
• Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K)
 
• Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba)
 
• Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I)
 
 
 
• Dobereiner's triads were an important step in the development of the periodic table, as they provided early evidence that elements could be grouped based on their properties and atomic masses.
 
• Although Dobereiner's triads were limited to a small number of elements, they paved the way for further classification schemes, eventually leading to Dmitri Mendeleev's periodic table.

questions.question: Which of the following has invented the musical instrument Bamhum and Tikzik?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moa Subong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Moa Subong** is a renowned musician from Nagaland, India.
 
• He is a member of the famous folk-fusion band **Abiogenesis**.
 
• Moa Subong is credited with the invention of two unique musical instruments, namely the **Bamhum** and **Tikzik**.
 
• The Bamhum is a bamboo-based wind instrument, while the Tikzik is a percussion instrument, both contributing to the innovative sound of Abiogenesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abiogenesis**

 
 
• Abiogenesis is a folk-fusion band from Nagaland, India, known for blending traditional Naga folk music with modern musical styles.
 
• The band was formed in 2005 and has gained recognition for their unique sound and musical innovation.
 
• Abiogenesis has performed at various national and international platforms, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of Nagaland.
 
• The band's music often features traditional Naga instruments along with modern instruments, creating a distinct fusion genre.
 
 
 
• **Bamhum**
 
 
• The Bamhum is a wind instrument made from bamboo, invented by Moa Subong.
 
• It produces a unique sound that is integral to the music of Abiogenesis.
 
• The Bamhum has been recognized for its innovation and contribution to folk music.
 
• It is played by blowing into it and using finger holes to create different notes and melodies.
 
 
 
• **Tikzik**
 
 
• The Tikzik is a percussion instrument also invented by Moa Subong.
 
• It adds rhythmic elements to the music of Abiogenesis, complementing the melodies of the Bamhum.
 
• The Tikzik is played by striking it with hands or sticks, producing a range of percussive sounds.
 
• It is crafted using traditional techniques and materials, reflecting the cultural heritage of Nagaland.

questions.question: From which date, Indian Financial year begins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st April**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Financial Year begins on **1st April** and ends on **31st March** of the next year.
 
• This accounting period is used by the Government of India and most businesses to prepare financial statements and reports.
 
• The financial year starting from 1st April aligns with the agricultural cycle in India, facilitating better planning and budgeting for the government and businesses.
 
• This timeline is also followed for the implementation of the government's fiscal policies and budgetary allocations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Year**

 
 
• A financial year, also known as a fiscal year, is a period used for calculating annual financial statements in businesses and other organizations.
 
• In India, the financial year starts on 1st April and ends on 31st March of the following year.
 
• This period is used by the government for budgeting and by companies for financial reporting and tax assessment.
 
 
 
• **Budget**
 
 
• The budget is a financial plan for a defined period, often one year.
 
• It is used by governments and organizations to manage income and expenditure.
 
• The Union Budget of India, which is presented annually on 1st February, outlines the revenue and expenditure for the upcoming financial year starting from 1st April.
 
 
 
• **Accounting Period**
 
 
• An accounting period is a span of time at the end of which financial statements are prepared to measure the financial performance of an entity.
 
• In India, the standard accounting period is the financial year from 1st April to 31st March.
 
• This period ensures uniformity and consistency in financial reporting and tax assessment.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policies**
 
 
• Fiscal policies refer to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions.
 
• These policies are planned and executed in alignment with the financial year to achieve economic goals like growth, employment, and inflation control.
 
• The financial year timeline helps in systematic planning and implementation of these policies.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors is the most labour absorbing sector of the economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Agriculture is the most labor-absorbing sector in many developing countries, including India.
 
• A significant portion of the rural population is engaged in agricultural activities, providing employment to a large number of people.
 
• It includes a variety of activities such as crop production, livestock rearing, forestry, and fishing.
 
• The sector is crucial for the livelihood of millions of people, especially in rural areas where other employment opportunities are limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agriculture**

 
 
• Agriculture involves the cultivation of plants and rearing of animals for food, fiber, medicinal plants, and other products used to sustain and enhance human life.
 
• It plays a vital role in the economy by providing raw materials to industries, contributing to GDP, and ensuring food security.
 
• Technological advancements and government policies significantly impact agricultural productivity and employment.
 
 
 
• **Industry**
 
 
• The industrial sector includes manufacturing, mining, construction, and utilities.
 
• It contributes to economic development by creating jobs, generating income, and fostering innovation.
 
• However, it is less labor-intensive compared to agriculture, especially with the advent of automation and mechanization.
 
 
 
• **Service**
 
 
• The service sector includes a wide range of activities such as retail, healthcare, education, finance, and information technology.
 
• It is a major contributor to GDP in many economies and has seen significant growth in recent years.
 
• While it provides numerous employment opportunities, it often requires higher skill levels and education compared to agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Banking**
 
 
• The banking sector is a subset of the service industry that deals with the management of financial transactions, savings, and investments.
 
• It plays a crucial role in economic stability and growth by providing credit and financial services to individuals and businesses.
 
• Employment in banking typically requires specialized knowledge and qualifications, making it less labor-intensive compared to agriculture.

questions.question: Who won the ICC ODI World Cup 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won the ICC ODI World Cup 2011 by defeating Sri Lanka in the final match.
 
• The final was held on April 2, 2011, at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.
 
• India chased down a target of 275 runs set by Sri Lanka, with a winning score of 277/4 in 48.2 overs.
 
• MS Dhoni, the captain of the Indian team, played a crucial unbeaten knock of 91* and was awarded the Man of the Match.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC ODI World Cup**

 
 
• The International Cricket Council (ICC) organizes the Cricket World Cup, which is the premier international championship of men's One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• The tournament is held every four years, featuring teams from around the world competing for the coveted trophy.
 
• The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975.
 
• Australia holds the record for the most World Cup wins, having clinched the title five times as of 2023.
 
 
 
• **Wankhede Stadium**
 
 
• Located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, Wankhede Stadium is one of the most iconic cricket stadiums in the world.
 
• The stadium was established in 1974 and has a seating capacity of around 33,000 spectators.
 
• It has hosted numerous important cricket matches, including the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup final.
 
• The stadium is known for its passionate cricket fans and electrifying atmosphere during matches.
 
 
 
• **MS Dhoni**
 
 
• Mahendra Singh Dhoni, commonly known as MS Dhoni, is a former Indian cricketer and captain of the Indian national team.
 
• He is renowned for his calm demeanor, strategic acumen, and finishing abilities in limited-overs cricket.
 
• Under his captaincy, India won several major ICC trophies, including the T20 World Cup in 2007, the ODI World Cup in 2011, and the Champions Trophy in 2013.
 
• Dhoni is regarded as one of the greatest captains and wicket-keeper batsmen in the history of cricket.
 
 
 
• **Man of the Match**
 
 
• The Man of the Match award is given to the player who has the most significant impact on the game, often contributing to his team's victory.
 
• In the 2011 ICC World Cup final, MS Dhoni was awarded the Man of the Match for his match-winning innings of 91* runs.
 
• This award is a recognition of the player's outstanding performance in a particular match.
 
• It is a prestigious accolade that highlights a player's contribution to the team's success.

questions.question: What is the time period of the rolling plan during the five-year plan in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1978 - 80**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rolling plan was introduced during the tenure of the Janata Party government in India.
 
• It was implemented after the termination of the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979).
 
• The rolling plan aimed at annual review and revision of the plan to adapt to the changing economic conditions and requirements.
 
• The rolling plan was in operation from 1978 to 1980 until it was replaced by the Sixth Five-Year Plan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on agricultural development.
 
• The plans aimed at strategic economic development and resource allocation.
 
• The Planning Commission of India was responsible for formulating and overseeing the plans.
 
 
 
• **Rolling Plan:**
 
 
• The rolling plan concept was introduced to allow flexibility and annual adjustments to the plans.
 
• It was an alternative to the rigid five-year framework, providing scope for course corrections based on economic performance and changing priorities.
 
• The rolling plan covered a period of two years from 1978 to 1980.
 
• It was eventually replaced by the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985) when the Congress government returned to power.

questions.question: In July 2023, who has been awarded the British Prime Minister's Points of Light award for volunteering several sustainability initiatives, including raising funds for children, since the age of three?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moksha Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Moksha Roy is a young environmental activist who has been volunteering in various sustainability initiatives since the age of three.
 
• She has been awarded the British Prime Minister's Points of Light award for her exceptional voluntary service and dedication to sustainability.
 
• Among her initiatives, she has raised funds for children and actively participated in numerous environmental campaigns.
 
• Her efforts have been recognized internationally, highlighting the impact of youth in driving positive environmental change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Points of Light Award:**

 
 
• The Points of Light award was established by former US President George H.W. Bush in 1990 to recognize outstanding volunteer service.
 
• It is awarded to individuals who make a significant difference in their communities through voluntary efforts.
 
• The British Prime Minister's Points of Light award follows a similar model to honor volunteers in the UK and abroad.
 
• The award showcases the powerful impact that individuals can make through dedication and volunteerism.
 
 
 
• **Sustainability Initiatives:**
 
 
• Sustainability initiatives refer to actions and projects aimed at promoting environmental conservation and reducing ecological footprints.
 
• These initiatives often include activities like recycling, tree planting, energy conservation, and advocating for sustainable practices.
 
• Sustainability is crucial for ensuring that natural resources are available for future generations.
 
• Youth engagement in sustainability initiatives is vital as it fosters a sense of responsibility and innovation in addressing environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Volunteering:**
 
 
• Volunteering involves offering time and services to benefit others without financial gain.
 
• It plays a critical role in community building, social cohesion, and addressing societal needs.
 
• Volunteers can work in various sectors, including education, health, environment, and social services.
 
• Recognition awards like the Points of Light highlight the importance and impact of volunteer work in society.

questions.question: Which Indian dancer won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Manipuri Dance in 2018?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akham Lakshmi Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Akham Lakshmi Devi** is a renowned Indian dancer known for her expertise in Manipuri dance.
 
• She was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2018 for her significant contribution to Manipuri dance.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of the highest Indian recognitions given to practicing artists.
 
• Her dedication and excellence in the art form have earned her national and international recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**

 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, also known as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar, is an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India’s National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• It is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists, gurus, and scholars in the field of performing arts.
 
• The award was established in 1952 and is given annually to artists in the field of music, dance, and drama.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a purse of Rs. 1,00,000, a shawl, and a tamrapatra (a brass plaque).
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Dance**
 
 
• Manipuri dance is one of the major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, which are usually performed to the accompaniment of traditional Manipuri music.
 
• Manipuri dance has a strong connection with the traditions and rituals of the people of Manipur, and it is often performed during religious and cultural festivals.
 
• The dance form includes various styles such as Ras Leela, Pung Cholom, and Thang Ta, among others.
 
 
 
• **Other notable awardees in 2018**
 
 
• Dr. Aruna Mohanty: She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contributions to Odissi dance.
 
• Gopika Varma: She is known for her contributions to Mohiniyattam dance.
 
• Surupa Sen: She received the award for her contributions to contemporary dance.

questions.question: What does "LBW" stand for in cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leg Before Wicket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leg Before Wicket (LBW) is one of the ways a batsman can be dismissed in the sport of cricket.
 
• The rule is designed to prevent the batsman from using their legs to block the ball from hitting the stumps.
 
• The umpire decides if the batsman is out LBW based on specific criteria defined in the cricket laws.
 
• The LBW decision involves the ball pitching in line with the stumps, not pitching outside the leg stump, and the ball hitting any part of the batsman's body before hitting the bat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Last Ball Wicket:**

 
 
• This term does not exist in official cricket terminology.
 
• It may refer to a wicket taken on the last ball of an over or the innings, but it is not an official term.
 
 
 
• **Leg Before Wicket (LBW):**
 
 
• This is a legitimate method of dismissing a batsman in cricket.
 
• For a batsman to be given out LBW, the ball must either be pitching in line with the stumps or outside off-stump, and it must impact the batsman in line with the stumps.
 
• The ball must also be predicted to hit the stumps if it had not hit the batsman's leg.
 
 
 
• **Long Boundary Wicket:**
 
 
• This term is not recognized in cricket terminology.
 
• It may be a misinterpretation or a colloquial term but has no official standing in cricket rules.
 
 
 
• **Leg Break Wrist:**
 
 
• This term could refer to the type of delivery bowled by a leg-spin bowler.
 
• Leg break refers to the ball spinning from the leg side to the off side for a right-handed batsman.
 
• However, it does not pertain to the method of dismissal.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Constitution guarantees six fundamental rights to its citizens.
 
• The rights mentioned are Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• There is no fundamental right called "Right to exploitation"; the correct term is "Right against Exploitation".
 
• The Right against Exploitation prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality:**

 
 
• It includes equality before law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom:**
 
 
• It includes freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association or union, movement, residence, and the right to practice any profession or occupation.
 
• Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation:**
 
 
• It prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.
 
• Articles 23 and 24 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion:**
 
 
• It ensures religious freedom and secularism in India.
 
• Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution cover this right.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:**
 
 
• It allows individuals to go to the courts for enforcement of the fundamental rights against the state.
 
• Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution cover this right.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the festival Vishu celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vishu is an important festival in the state of **Kerala**, celebrated with great enthusiasm and joy.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Malayalam New Year and is observed in the month of April.
 
• The festival is known for the ritual of 'Vishukkani,' which means "the first thing seen on Vishu."
 
• Traditional customs include lighting lamps and seeing auspicious items like rice, fruits, and flowers first thing in the morning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vishu**

 
 
• Vishu is one of the major festivals celebrated in Kerala and parts of Tamil Nadu. It is similar to the festival of Baisakhi in Punjab, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, and Bihu in Assam.
 
• The festival is characterized by the ritualistic arrangement of ‘Vishukkani,’ which includes items like rice, lemon, cucumber, coconut, jackfruit, kanikkonna (golden shower flower), betel leaves, areca nut, metal mirror, and coins.
 
• Another significant aspect of Vishu is the 'Vishukkaineetam,' where elders of the family give money to the younger members as a token of blessings.
 
• A special feast called 'Sadya' is prepared on this day, featuring a variety of traditional dishes served on a banana leaf.
 
 
 
• **Malayalam Calendar**
 
 
• The Malayalam calendar, also known as Kollavarsham, is a solar calendar used in Kerala. Vishu marks the first day of Medam, the ninth month of the Malayalam calendar.
 
• This calendar is used for various religious, cultural, and agricultural purposes in Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Vishukkani**
 
 
• The term 'Vishukkani' literally means the first sight on Vishu day. It is a traditional arrangement of auspicious items meant to be viewed first thing in the morning to bring prosperity and good luck.
 
• The arrangement is usually done the night before Vishu, and family members view it early in the morning, often with closed eyes until they reach the spot where the Vishukkani is set up.
 
 
 
• **Vishukkaineetam**
 
 
• Vishukkaineetam is a custom where elders give money to younger members of the family and other dependents. This is considered a gesture of blessing and goodwill.
 
• It is believed that receiving Vishukkaineetam brings prosperity and luck for the entire year.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dance form of Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is a traditional folk dance of Assam that is performed during the Bihu festival, which marks the Assamese New Year.
 
• Bihu dance is characterized by brisk dance steps, rapid hand movements, and rhythmic beats played on traditional instruments like the dhol and pepa.
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women, dressed in traditional Assamese attire, which includes colorful mekhela chadors for women and dhotis and gamosas for men.
 
• Bihu dance is not just a form of entertainment but also a way to express joy and celebrate the spirit of unity and prosperity among the Assamese people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghoomar**

 
 
• Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is performed by women in swirling robes and is known for its graceful movements and vibrant costumes.
 
• The dance is performed to the folk tunes of traditional instruments like the dhol, nagada, and flute.
 
• Ghoomar is usually performed during festive occasions and celebrations such as weddings and religious events.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India.
 
• It is known for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and expressive gestures.
 
• Kathakali performances are based on stories from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
 
• The dance involves highly stylized movements and facial expressions, accompanied by music and vocalists.
 
 
 
• **Garba**
 
 
• Garba is a traditional folk dance from Gujarat, India.
 
• It is performed during the Navratri festival and involves rhythmic clapping and circular movements.
 
• Garba is usually performed in groups, and participants wear colorful traditional attire.
 
• The dance is accompanied by live music featuring instruments like the dhol, tabla, and harmonium.

questions.question: In January 2023, who has been appointed as the Director General in the Directorate of General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Dev Dutt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vikram Dev Dutt was appointed as the Director General in the Directorate of General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) in January 2023.
 
• Prior to this appointment, he served as the Chairman and Managing Director of Air India Assets Holding Ltd (AIAHL).
 
• Vikram Dev Dutt is an IAS officer of the 1993 batch from the AGMUT cadre.
 
• He has held various key positions in the government, including roles in the Ministry of Civil Aviation and other important departments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)**

 
 
• The DGCA is the regulatory body in the field of Civil Aviation, primarily dealing with safety issues. It is responsible for the regulation of air transport services to/from/within India and for the enforcement of civil air regulations, air safety, and airworthiness standards.
 
• The DGCA also coordinates all regulatory functions with the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).
 
• The headquarters of DGCA is located in New Delhi, India.
 
• It oversees the issuance of licenses to pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, air traffic controllers, and other personnel, as well as the certification of airports.
 
 
 
• **Air India Assets Holding Ltd (AIAHL)**
 
 
• AIAHL is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) set up by the Government of India to hold the debt and non-core assets of Air India.
 
• The objective of AIAHL is to clean up the financials of Air India before its strategic disinvestment.
 
• The SPV manages and monetizes the assets transferred to it from Air India to repay the liabilities.
 
 
 
• **International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO)**
 
 
• ICAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations, established in 1944 to manage the administration and governance of the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention).
 
• It works with the Convention’s 193 Member States and global aviation organizations to develop policies and standards, undertake compliance audits, perform studies and analyses, provide assistance and build aviation capacity through various projects and programs.
 
• ICAO’s mission is to promote the safe and orderly development of international civil aviation worldwide.

questions.question: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in _________ language and were written in the _________ script.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakrit, Brahmi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in the **Prakrit language**, which was the lingua franca of the time.
 
• The inscriptions were primarily written in the **Brahmi script**, which is one of the oldest writing systems used in ancient India.
 
• Ashoka's use of the Prakrit language and Brahmi script made his messages accessible to a larger audience, including the common people.
 
• These inscriptions were meant to spread the Buddhist teachings and Ashoka's policies of dharma (moral law).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prakrit Language**

 
 
• Prakrit refers to a group of Middle Indo-Aryan languages that were spoken in ancient India. It was the vernacular language of the people, in contrast to the classical Sanskrit used by the elite.
 
• Prakrits were used extensively in literature, inscriptions, and religious texts, especially in Jainism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script**
 
 
• The Brahmi script is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia and is the ancestor of most modern Indian scripts.
 
• It was used from the 3rd century BCE and is best known from the inscriptions of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• It is an abugida, meaning that each symbol represents a consonant with an inherent vowel, which can be changed with diacritics.
 
• The script was deciphered in the 19th century by James Prinsep, which was a significant milestone in the study of Indian epigraphy.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka's Inscriptions**
 
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are a series of edicts on rocks and pillars that were issued by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Dynasty during his reign in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• These inscriptions are found across the Indian subcontinent and are written in various languages including Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic, but Prakrit is the most common.
 
• The inscriptions serve as an important source of information about Ashoka's policies, his conversion to Buddhism, and his efforts to spread Buddhist philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script**
 
 
• Kharosthi is another ancient script used in the northwestern regions of India and Central Asia, contemporary with Brahmi.
 
• It is written from right to left, unlike Brahmi which is written from left to right.
 
• While Brahmi was used for the majority of Ashoka's inscriptions, a few inscriptions in the northwest were written in Kharosthi.
